section: 1. the daemons: who does what
text: Daemon Runs on Does If it dies slurmctld the controller one head node (plus optional backups) holds every job, node, partition and reservation in memory; runs the schedulers; answers every sbatch , squeue , scontrol ; saves its state to StateSaveLocation so a restart loses nothing running jobs keep running (their processes live on the nodes); nothing new starts and commands fail until it is back or a backup controller (a second SlurmctldHost line) takes over after SlurmctldTimeout (default 120 s) slurmd every compute node, as root registers the node (CPUs, memory, GRES), starts job steps, runs the prolog and epilog, reports back after SlurmdTimeout without an answer (default 300 s) the controller marks the node DOWN and requeues or kills its jobs slurmstepd one per step per node, started by slurmd starts the step's tasks, tracks every process they fork, applies the cgroup limits, collects usage, forwards stdout to srun its step fails slurmdbd + a MariaDB/MySQL database usually the head node the accounting database: every job's usage (what sacct and fairshare read), users, accounts, QOS and their limits the controller queues records and keeps scheduling; new limits and users cannot be changed until it returns munged every node authentication: every message carries a credential sealed with a key that every node shares nothing on that node can talk to Slurm Defaults read from src/common/read_config.h at slurm-24-11-5-1: .

text: Any reason: How to read a limit name The 170 limit reasons follow one grammar, and the decoder above splits any of them: who ( Assoc : your user or account association; QOS : the job's QOS; ...PerAccount / ...PerUser without a prefix: a QOS limit counted per account or user), kind ( Grp : the sum over all running jobs of that association or QOS; Max : one job, or one user or node, as the suffix says; Min : a minimum the job does not meet), resource ( Cpu , Mem / Memory , Node , GRES (GPUs), Billing , Energy , License , BB (burst buffer), Jobs , SubmitJobs , Wall ), and measure (nothing: the amount held now; Minutes : resource-minutes used, including finished jobs; RunMinutes : resource-minutes still to run for jobs running now, from their time limits).
